items.blurb: Run by volunteers of the Columbia County Museum Association, the museum tells the county's story through displays on shipping, railroads, farming, schools, the military and logging, with a genealogy research library for family historians.
items.name: Columbia County Museum

items.blurb: Built in 1919 as St. Helens Elementary School after a fire took the earlier school, this contributing building of the St. Helens Downtown Historic District was restored and reopened in 2024 as a civic center — and won a 2025 DeMuro Award for excellence in historic preservation.
items.name: John Gumm Building

items.blurb: Built in 1906 of locally quarried basalt in the Colonial Revival style, the courthouse at 230 Strand Street anchors the historic downtown plaza on the St. Helens riverfront.
items.name: Columbia County Courthouse

items.blurb: Roughly ten riverfront blocks of homes, civic buildings and storefronts listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984 — the historic heart of Olde Towne St. Helens.
items.name: St. Helens Downtown Historic District (Olde Towne)

items.blurb: Olde Towne's historic movie theatre, built in 1928 and still showing films on the St. Helens riverfront.
items.name: Columbia Theatre

items.blurb: Built in 1870 by Dr. Charles Caples, Columbia County's first physician, this Columbia City home was bequeathed to the Daughters of the American Revolution as a museum in 1959 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2005.
items.name: Caples House Museum

items.blurb: The 1902 Victorian home of James Grant Watts, a Scappoose founding father and the town's first mayor, is now the Watts House Pioneer Museum, home of the Scappoose Historical Society and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
items.name: Watts House Pioneer Museum

items.blurb: A 22-mile trail from Scappoose to Vernonia following a logging railroad first built in 1906; interpretive signs along the way tell the county's logging and railroad story, and the trail was designated a National Recreation Trail in 2023.
items.name: Crown Zellerbach Trail

items.blurb: Established in 2015 on the top floor of Rainier City Hall, the museum collects, archives and shares the history of the Rainier area — photos, documents and artifacts of the river town's past.
items.name: Rainier Oregon Historical Museum

items.blurb: A fourteen-room house built in 1888 by George F. Moeck, a Rainier merchant and former mayor; it was placed on the National Register of Historic Places on April 14, 1978.
items.name: Moeck House — The 1888 House

items.blurb: Pioneer cemeteries in the Hudson community west of Rainier, listed together on the National Register of Historic Places in 2001; Woodbine was platted in 1893 and its earliest marked grave dates to 1879.
items.name: Woodbine & Green Mountain Cemeteries

items.blurb: Known as 'The Castle,' this National Register-listed mansion at 620 SW Tichenor Street was built in 1898–1902 by lumberman Thomas Flippin with timber from his own crews; the Clatskanie Historical Society Museum moved into its top floor in 2017.
items.name: Flippin House & Clatskanie Historical Society Museum

items.blurb: A 48-foot waterfall on Beaver Creek near Clatskanie, where the creek sheets over a basalt chute into a natural amphitheater; a 0.3-mile trail leads in from Beaver Falls Road.
items.name: Beaver Falls

items.blurb: Housed in the 1922 former headquarters of the Oregon-American Lumber Company, this volunteer-run museum opened during the 1963 Vernonia Jamboree and holds more than 5,000 items on the area's logging and pioneer life.
items.name: Vernonia Pioneer Museum
